01 · Get readyStep 01 / 28

Choose your starting point

A self-paced route from a small brief to a saved Unreal cinematic.

  1. Download and extract the Part 2 workshop ZIP from the class folder. Open Start Here.html in the extracted folder. Work on a copy, not inside a ZIP preview.
  2. Starting from scratch: use the Starter project. Exploring the completed work: use the Finished project and open Unreal/PaperCity.uproject. Keep the original download as your recovery copy.
  3. You can follow every numbered step without Alex. The slide deck is the teaching view; this workbook contains the full instructions. Last week’s kit is optional because the source Paper City scene is included.
Small Worlds · Part 2
Actions/    Run these inside Unreal
Unreal/     PaperCity.uproject
SourceAssets/  Part 1 scene
Studio/     Design + your notes
Recipes/    Reference + recovery

Check your work

The folder contains Actions, Unreal, SourceAssets, Studio and Recipes. Studio/design.json identifies brief SW-18.

If you get stuck

If you only see a web preview, extract the complete folder. If you missed Part 1, use the included files and begin here.

01 · Get readyStep 02 / 28

Bring one assistant and Unreal

Use the account you already have.

  1. Open Codex or Claude Desktop in its local coding workspace. Sign in to an account that can read and edit a local folder. An account subscription may be needed; no paid API key is required by this workshop.
  2. Install Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview using Epic Games Launcher if available to your account and operating system. This edition was prepared for 5.9.0 Preview, changelist 60351404. Allow time for the large download.
  3. Keep a working older Unreal installation. A 5.9-saved project is not an older-version starter. If your platform lacks this Preview, follow the workbook and inspect the reference media; do not convert your only production project.

Get Unreal EngineGet CodexGet Claude Desktop

Target: Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview
One local coding assistant
No headset
No paid asset pack
No paid API key

Prompt to copy

Read only: identify my operating system, installed Unreal versions, available space and whether this app can access the workshop folder. Report what is verified and what needs a local check. Do not install software or change my other projects.

Check your work

You know the exact engine you will open and the local workshop location.

If you get stuck

If 5.9 is unavailable, stop the native steps here and read the reference route. Do not claim the Unreal scripts ran in a browser or in system Python.

01 · Get readyStep 04 / 28

Write a small job before running it

Give the agent a finish line it can check.

  1. Open Studio/job-template.md. Replace the bracketed fields with your own goal and limits. Use the sample goal below if this is your first attempt.
  2. Permit edits only in this workshop copy. Choose a time limit, a retry limit and whether new downloads or paid services are allowed.
  3. Ask for a plan before the first write. Read it and authorize the bounded job. The assistant must report actual evidence rather than filling in a successful receipt in advance.
Goal
Inputs + allowed files
Budget + retry limit
Checkpoint + recovery
Evidence + your verdict

Prompt to copy

Draft Studio/my-job.md for this goal: build Paper City in Unreal, make a dusk variant, add a lantern festival and create a 12-second sequence. Only use this workshop and built-in Unreal assets. Budget: 30 minutes of active agent work, at most two retries per failed step, no paid services or downloads. Preserve prior maps. Finish with saved maps, verification output and a list of visual checks for me. Show the plan before running it.

Check your work

The job names allowed files, budget, stop conditions and the output you will inspect.

If you get stuck

Shrink a broad request such as “make it amazing” to one visible change with a comparison image. Keep stretch ideas in a separate list.

01 · Get readyStep 05 / 28

Open the supplied Unreal project

A Blueprint-only project avoids a compiler setup.

  1. In the Starter copy, double-click Unreal/PaperCity.uproject and choose your installed 5.9 Preview editor. If Windows asks which app to use, open the engine first and browse to the project.
  2. The project requests Python Editor Script Plugin, Editor Scripting Utilities, Sequencer Scripting and Movie Render Queue. If prompted, enable them and restart this project. Do not build an engine from source.
  3. On a fresh starter the final map does not exist yet. An empty editor or missing startup-map notice is expected. Open the Output Log from Window → Developer Tools → Output Log (or search the Window menu).
PaperCity.uproject
Blueprint-only
Built-in editor plugins
No third-party plugin required

Prompt to copy

Help me open only Unreal/PaperCity.uproject with my installed 5.9 Preview. Verify the engine version and these enabled plugins: Python Editor Script Plugin, Editor Scripting Utilities, Sequencer Scripting and Movie Render Queue. Do not convert any other project or install C++ tools.

Check your work

You have the PaperCity editor open and an Output Log with no missing required plugin error.

If you get stuck

If the project asks to compile C++ or reports a third-party plugin, you opened the wrong folder. This project has no C++ module and requires no AI bridge plugin.

01 · Get readyStep 06 / 28

Run a harmless Python check

Unreal Python runs inside the editor.

  1. In the Output Log input, keep the normal console command mode and enter: py import unreal; print(unreal.SystemLibrary.get_engine_version()). Press Enter.
  2. Look for the printed engine version in the log. A system terminal cannot import Unreal’s editor module.
  3. For action files, use Tools → Execute Python Script and browse to the numbered file in Actions. If that menu is absent, use the console form: py "FULL/PATH/TO/Actions/00_check_environment.py". Replace FULL/PATH/TO with your extracted workshop location; use forward slashes.
Output Log console
py "…/Actions/00_check_environment.py"
Expected: SMALL_WORLDS_ENVIRONMENT

Prompt to copy

Explain how to run Actions/00_check_environment.py inside my already-open Unreal editor. Give me the exact py command with my local file path, using forward slashes. Do not run it in system Python. Wait for me to paste its log result.

Check your work

The log prints SMALL_WORLDS_ENVIRONMENT with the engine version and workshop path.

If you get stuck

If you see “No module named unreal”, the command ran in the wrong Python. If the script file is missing, remove the ZIP from the path and select the extracted Actions file.

02 · Build the worldStep 07 / 28

Build the daylight baseline

Generate native actors from a readable recipe.

  1. In Unreal choose Tools → Execute Python Script and select Actions/01_build_starter.py. This creates /Game/SmallWorlds/Maps/01_PaperCity.
  2. Wait for SMALL_WORLDS_PASS in Output Log. In Content Browser open Content → SmallWorlds → Maps. Double-click 01_PaperCity if necessary.
  3. In the Outliner search SW_Tower. Count three towers. Select SW_Cam_Wide and use Pilot from its context menu to inspect the overall composition. Press Ctrl+S / Cmd+S to save.
01_PaperCity
Three towers
Two bridges
Canal + lanterns
Saved baseline

Prompt to copy

Read the starter builder and Studio/design.json. Explain what Actions/01_build_starter.py will create and how it avoids replacing an existing map. Then give me its exact Unreal console command. After I run it, help me inspect the actual log and actor list.

Check your work

Three towers, two bridges, a canal, lamps and a cyan sculpture are visible. The log records the map and actor count.

If you get stuck

If it says the map already exists, open it instead of rerunning. Preserve it by copying the whole workshop before a fresh build. If a script fails, read the first traceback before retrying.

02 · Build the worldStep 08 / 28

Check scale before polishing

Unreal scene units are centimeters.

  1. Select SW_Tower_1, SW_Tower_2 and SW_Tower_3 in the Outliner. Their cube scales are Z=2, Z=3 and Z=4 because the source cube is 100 cm high.
  2. Compare the two 180 cm-wide bridges with the towers. Do not infer real-world height from the viewport zoom.
  3. Run Actions/05_verify_current.py. Keep its actual JSON result in Studio/receipts. The verifier checks structure and dimensions; you still inspect the picture.
100 cm cube × Z scale
2 = 200 cm
3 = 300 cm
4 = 400 cm

Prompt to copy

Check the three SW_Tower actors against Studio/design.json. Explain the difference between source-mesh size, actor scale and world-space height. Report the measured values from Unreal if connected; otherwise ask me for the Details values. Do not claim you inspected the editor from source code alone.

Check your work

Tower heights are 200 / 300 / 400 cm. A receipt states the engine and actor count.

If you get stuck

A 100× scale error means meters and centimeters were confused. Fix only a duplicate project, then rerun verification and inspect the framing.

02 · Build the worldStep 09 / 28

Inspect the material library

Separate the shape from its surface.

  1. Open Content → SmallWorlds → Materials. Open M_Jade and inspect Base Color, Roughness and Metallic in the graph.
  2. Select a bridge rail, inspect its material slot and confirm it uses M_Jade. Compare the rough paper towers with the glossier canal.
  3. Ask your assistant for one bounded material variation. Duplicate the material in Content Browser before editing. Apply the duplicate to one selected rail and compare it with the untouched bridge.
Mesh → material slot
Base Color
Roughness
Metallic
Duplicate before editing

Prompt to copy

Propose one jade-rail material variation with an exact Base Color, Roughness and Metallic value. Keep the paper walls and canal unchanged. Tell me how to duplicate M_Jade and apply the duplicate to only one bridge rail. I will inspect before accepting it.

Check your work

One rail uses your duplicate material; the original M_Jade and the other bridge stay available for comparison.

If you get stuck

If every rail changed, you edited the shared material. Restore its prior values, duplicate it and apply the duplicate to a single actor.

Make a dusk lighting variant

Change the light while preserving the daylight map.

  1. Run Actions/02_build_dusk.py. It creates 02_Dusk as a separate map with warmer key light, emissive lanterns and point lights.
  2. Open 01_PaperCity and 02_Dusk in turn. Use the same SW_Cam_Wide view for both. Wait for shader compilation and exposure to settle.
  3. Capture both views with the same viewport size using your operating system screenshot tool. Save them in Studio/evidence and record which version you prefer.
01_PaperCity → baseline
02_Dusk → warm lamps
Same camera + same crop
Your visual verdict

Prompt to copy

Read the two stage definitions. Before I run 02_build_dusk.py, predict which lighting settings will change. After I supply matching screenshots and the log, compare shadow direction, lantern visibility, highlights and tower readability. Separate observations from suggestions.

Check your work

Both maps exist. The dusk view has visible warm lanterns and readable towers. Your verdict is recorded with the compared filenames.

If you get stuck

If the view is black, confirm you are looking through a camera, not below the plinth. Check exposure and lights in the saved map before raising every intensity.

Turn one prop into a reusable recipe

A lantern has a small, understandable construction.

  1. In small_worlds.py find the loop that creates SW_LanternPost, SW_LanternCap, SW_Lantern and SW_LanternLight. Read the dimensions and labels together.

  3. Have it write the recipe into Studio/prop-proposal.md before it edits code. Require a unique actor prefix so the result can be found and removed as one scoped experiment.

Give feedback the agent can act on

Name the visual problem and protect what works.

  1. Pick one screenshot and write what you see. Example: “The hanging lanterns overlap the middle tower’s windows.”
  2. Name the protected elements: tower heights, camera, bridge width and accepted rail material. Limit the edit to one prop group.
  3. Ask for one revision in a duplicate map. Capture the same camera again. Accept or reject the visible result rather than the assistant’s confidence.
Observation
One allowed change
Protected choices
Same comparison view
Accept or reject

Prompt to copy

The hanging lanterns overlap the middle tower windows in my attached view. Propose a single change to their height or spacing. Preserve tower heights, both bridges, the camera and all materials. Work only in a duplicate named 03_LanternFestival_MyRevision. Explain the comparison I should inspect before editing.

Check your work

The revision changes one named problem and preserves your protected choices.

If you get stuck

If the agent rewrites the whole scene, stop it, restore the duplicate from your baseline and restate the exact actor prefix it may change.

Request a batch with a fixed budget

Make several ideas, then choose.

  1. Ask for three written variations first: quiet gallery, night market and sculptural park. Keep the towers and bridges as shared constraints.
  2. Choose one to build in a separate map. Limit the job to a fixed prop count and a small number of material colors.
  3. Require the output list and a screenshot before the agent starts another variation. A batch is a set of reviewable alternatives, not permission for endless generation.
Quiet gallery
Night market
Sculpture park
Choose → build → inspect

Prompt to copy

Propose three variants of Paper City: quiet gallery, night market and sculpture park. For each, give exactly three prop families, a three-color palette and one hero-camera idea. Use built-in geometry. Do not build yet. I will choose one, then authorize at most 12 new props in a separate map with a 10-minute budget.

Three distinct proposals can be compared before using compute or changing files.

03 · Direct the AIStep 15 / 28

Compare with the original Blender scene

Understand what survived the engine handoff.

  1. Open SourceAssets/Paper City.blend in Blender if installed, or inspect the included source postcard. This is the Part 1 starting scene, not a claim about every live-class edit.
  2. The native Unreal recipe is a deliberate reinterpretation: three towers, folded roofs, a canal and jade rails, expanded into a festival. It is not a lossless import.
  3. Optional: drag SourceAssets/Paper City.glb into an empty Content Browser folder in a duplicate project. Review the import options, scale, materials and hierarchy. Compare imported geometry with the native recipe; do not replace the finished map.
Source scene → handoff
Units + axes
Materials + hierarchy
Rebuild ≠ lossless import

Prompt to copy

Compare the included Part 1 source assets with the Unreal construction recipe. Identify what is preserved, what is rebuilt and what needs checking after a GLB import: units, axes, material slots, transparency and object hierarchy. Do not call the native reconstruction a lossless import.

Check your work

You can distinguish an imported mesh from a native reconstruction and list the handoff checks.

If you get stuck

If GLB import is unavailable in your editor configuration, keep it optional. The main workshop uses built-in Unreal meshes and does not depend on that importer.

03 · Direct the AIStep 16 / 28

Choose how AI reaches the editor

The same job can use a script or a direct tool connection.

  1. The required path uses the local coding assistant to prepare files and you to run the numbered script in Unreal. It works without a third-party bridge.
  2. An instructor with an installed, tested ue5-mcp connection can inspect actors, edit the scene and capture it directly. Ask for a read-only actor query first, then one bounded write in a duplicate map.
  3. UE 5.9 also includes experimental native tool infrastructure. Installed plugins determine which tools are present. Do not assume the built-in server exposes every operation from another bridge.
Local assistant → script → Unreal
Connected assistant → native tools → Unreal
Both need visible verification

Prompt to copy

First tell me which Unreal tools this chat actually has. If none, use the script-and-manual-run route. If connected, perform a read-only query for the current map and SW_Tower actors, report actual values and stop. Do not infer connectivity from a plugin file on disk.

Check your work

The agent identifies its actual connection and can show a real query result or clearly use the manual route.

If you get stuck

A server health response proves transport, not editing. Test one harmless read before giving write authority. Do not publish an unauthenticated editor port to the internet.

04 · Make it moveStep 17 / 28

Create the 12-second cinematic

Three shots and one animated sculpture.

  1. Run Actions/04_build_cinematic.py. It creates 04_Cinematic and Content/SmallWorlds/Cinematics/LS_LanternFestival.
  2. Open the new map, then double-click LS_LanternFestival in Content Browser. In Sequencer enable the camera-cut view button on the Camera Cuts track.
  3. Scrub frames 0, 96 and 192. You should see wide, bridge and sculpture cameras. Scrub between keys to inspect the floating sculpture and camera movement.
0–95 · Wide
96–191 · Bridge
192–287 · Sculpture
24 fps × 12 s = 288 frames

Prompt to copy

Explain Actions/04_build_cinematic.py before I run it. Identify the three camera cuts, the 24 fps frame ranges and the animated sculpture. After I run it, help me inspect the cut track and transform keys. Do not claim rendered motion from key counts alone.

Check your work

The sequence lasts 288 frames at 24 fps, with three four-second shots. The sculpture moves and rotates when scrubbed.

If you get stuck

If the viewport stays on your free camera, enable Sequencer’s camera-cut lock. If the sequence already exists, open it rather than overwriting it.

04 · Make it moveStep 18 / 28

Review the start, middle and end

A camera move must hold its composition.

  1. For the first shot inspect frames 0, 48 and 95. For the second inspect 96, 144 and 191. For the third inspect 192, 240 and 287.
  2. At each frame check the focal subject, foreground intersections, lantern visibility and whether the frame clips a roof or sculpture.
  3. If a move fails, duplicate the sequence and shorten its travel before adding more keys. Save nine frame captures or a contact sheet for your review.
Shot 1: 0 / 48 / 95
Shot 2: 96 / 144 / 191
Shot 3: 192 / 240 / 287

Prompt to copy

Make me a nine-frame inspection checklist for LS_LanternFestival: start, middle and end of each shot. For each, I will mark framing, clipping, focal subject and lighting. If a shot fails, propose the smallest camera-key adjustment and preserve the original sequence.

Check your work

All three samples in each shot have been inspected. A keyframe existing is separate from good composition.

If you get stuck

If a subject leaves the frame, reduce translation or retarget the end rotation in the duplicate sequence. Recheck all three samples.

04 · Make it moveStep 19 / 28

Render a short image sequence

Use frames first so a failed encode does not waste a render.

  1. Open Window → Cinematics → Movie Render Queue. Add LS_LanternFestival. Confirm the job’s map is 04_Cinematic.
  2. Open the job settings. Add or keep Deferred Rendering and PNG Sequence. In Output choose a new folder inside Studio/renders, set 1280 × 720 and 24 fps, and keep the sequence frame range. Use Anti-Aliasing engine warm-up if effects need time to initialize.
  3. Render locally. Wait for completion, then open the first, middle and last frames. Keep the Output Log if the render reports an error. The optional command-line encode recipe is in Recipes/04-render.md.
Map: 04_Cinematic
Sequence: LS_LanternFestival
1280 × 720 · 24 fps
PNG frames → inspect → encode

Prompt to copy

Help me configure one local Movie Render Queue job for LS_LanternFestival in map 04_Cinematic: 1280×720, 24 fps, PNG frames, a new Studio/renders folder and the sequence’s 288-frame range. Explain the settings I must inspect. Do not start an overnight render or overwrite prior frames.

Check your work

A new folder contains the rendered frame sequence. You inspected images from all three cuts.

If you get stuck

If every frame uses one camera, check the saved Camera Cuts track and job sequence. If the render is much brighter than the viewport, compare exposure and cinematic scalability before adjusting lights.

Turn frames into a review video

Inspect the movie after encoding.

  1. If FFmpeg is already installed, ask the assistant to inspect the actual image filenames and form an encode command from that pattern. Do not assume a filename that is not present.
  2. Use H.264, yuv420p and 24 fps for the review MP4. Keep the original frames and use a new output filename.
  3. Play the full movie. Check the cut boundaries and sculpture motion, then seek to the last frame. Record any visual defect separately from decode success.
Rendered frames
Actual filename pattern
H.264 · yuv420p · 24 fps
Decode + human viewing

Read the filenames in my Studio/renders folder. If FFmpeg is installed, encode the 24 fps PNG sequence to a new H.264 yuv420p MP4 without deleting frames or replacing another video. Show the exact input pattern. Validate decode, duration and dimensions, then ask me to inspect the complete movie.

Check your work

You have a playable review MP4 and an actual decode result. Your visual verdict names any remaining issue.

If you get stuck

If filenames contain gaps, repair the render or explicitly choose a correct continuous range. Do not hide missing frames by silently looping a still.

  3. Restore the correct key from the original design file. Use a fresh duplicate before running again because the failed action may already have created a partial map. Record the failure, repair and rerun result.

Give a longer job a real boundary

The finish line stays visible while you are away.

  1. Choose one extension you can verify: a new prop set, one lighting variation or one revised camera sequence.
  2. Specify the allowed map, output folder, maximum active time, retry count and checkpoint frequency. Name actions that require you, such as approving a paid generation or judging the final image.
  3. Ask for a short progress file at each completed milestone. A long-running process is not completion; the final receipt must name the saved output and known issues.
One extension
Exact files + map
Time + retries
Milestone evidence
Known limits
